page_title: Apolo · Free image optimizer: compress to WebP, AVIF and JPEG XL

sources.entry: Apolo - Open-source image optimizer that compresses and converts to WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL, JPEG and PNG, showing the loss and its SSIMULACRA 2 score before saving. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/webcafeina/Apolo) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Apolo
summary.one_liner: Apolo is a free, open-source image optimizer that compresses and converts photos to WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL, JPEG, PNG and QOI locally, showing the quality loss before you save.
use_cases: Shrinking photo file sizes before publishing on a website
Converting images to WebP or AVIF for faster web pages
Batch compressing a folder of photos
Comparing quality loss between compressed and original images
Converting iPhone HEIC photos to other formats
Compressing images without uploading them to a cloud service
summary.what_it_does: Apolo compresses and converts images to WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL, MozJPEG, PNG and QOI on the user's own computer, and it can open iPhone HEIC files. Before saving, it shows a slider, side-by-side view and difference map, with an SSIMULACRA 2 score for each result. It can search for the lowest quality setting that reaches a target score such as 80 on each photo. The page says its output matches the official tools (cwebp, cjpeg, oxipng, avifenc, cjxl) byte for byte and that users can copy the equivalent command. It also supports batch folder processing and includes a built-in MCP server for AI agents such as Claude, Cursor and VS Code.
notable: Shows SSIMULACRA 2 quality scores and visual diff before saving
Runs locally with no photo uploads
Byte-for-byte output matching official encoders like cwebp and cjxl
Built-in MCP server for AI agents
caveats: Your browser may not display JPEG XL previews; Safari does
Page does not state a license name beyond 'free and open source'; the awesome-mac listing marks it as open source and freeware
